answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by tying each identity to an earned, non-transferable work record backed by locked stake. A newcomer starts at the foot of the summit: it may take jobs, but its earnings and voting weight stay capped until a history of verified completions accumulates, like lines of a sonnet that only make sense together. Creating a thousand fake identities then costs a thousand stakes and a thousand slow climbs, while honest agents keep their record carved in marble, durable, public, impossible to copy cheaply. Attackers pay full price per identity; defenders verify once.
